note: Suggestions only. Feather never disables anything without your confirmation.

startup.r: Part of Windows Security. Disabling it hides protection warnings.
Security or privacy protection. Keep it unless you are replacing it with another product.
Windows text input service (keyboard layouts, handwriting, voice typing).
Adobe updater. Adobe apps keep working; check for updates from inside the app when you want them.
Adobe Creative Cloud background apps. Adobe programs still open without them; sync and update notices pause.
Keeps Chrome and other Google apps updated. Disabling can leave your browser out of date, which is a security risk.
Java updater. Java programs still run.
Music app. Starts with Windows only for convenience; open it yourself when needed.
Chat app. You can open it yourself when needed.
Game launcher. Open it yourself when you want to play.
Game launcher. Open it yourself when you want to play.
Game launcher. Open it yourself when you want to play.
Chat/calling app. Open it yourself when needed.
Chat/meeting app. Open it yourself when needed; you may miss message notifications until you do.
Meeting app. Open it yourself or from a meeting link.
Messaging app. Disabling means no notifications until you open it.
Torrent client. It only needs to run while you are downloading.
Apple helper for iTunes/iPod. iTunes still works when opened.
iCloud sync for photos and drive. Disabling pauses syncing until you open it.
File sync. Disabling stops syncing until you open Dropbox.
OneDrive file sync and backup of Desktop/Documents. Disabling stops syncing until you open it.
Google Drive sync. Disabling stops syncing until you open it.
CCleaner background monitoring/updater. Not needed for the PC to work.
Third-party 'optimizer' helper. Not needed for Windows; it mainly runs reminders and scans.
Voice assistant. Not needed for Windows to run.
Pre-loads Edge so it opens faster. Edge still works without it.
Updates Microsoft Edge. Disabling can leave the browser out of date.
Apple Bonjour discovery. Only needed by some Apple and printer software.
Browser helper or assistant. Not needed for the browser to work.
OneNote quick-capture helper. OneNote still works without it.
Updates Microsoft Office. Disabling can leave Office out of date.
Razer device software. Disabling can turn off keyboard/mouse lighting, macros and profiles.
Logitech device software. Disabling can turn off custom buttons and profiles.
Gaming device software. Disabling can turn off lighting, macros and profiles.
NVIDIA helper. The graphics driver itself is unaffected, but overlays, recording and driver notices may stop.
Intel graphics helper. Display hotkeys and some screen settings may stop working.
AMD graphics helper. Overlays and some display features may stop working.
Audio control software. Disabling can remove audio effects, headphone/jack detection or equalizer settings.
Touchpad driver helper. Gestures and settings may stop working.
Bluetooth helper. Bluetooth tray controls may stop working.
Pen tablet driver helper. Pen pressure and buttons may stop working.
PC maker utility. It may control hotkeys, battery or fan settings; check what it does before disabling.
Adds 7-Zip to the right-click menu. Disabling only removes those menu items.
Adds WinRAR to the right-click menu. Disabling only removes those menu items.
Right-click menu extension. Disabling only removes that menu entry.

services.r: Core Windows service. Disabling it can stop Windows, networking, security or sign-in from working.
Windows Update service. Disabling it stops security updates.
Fax service. Only needed if you send faxes from this PC.
Lets other computers change this PC's registry. Disabling is safer for most people.
Connected User Experiences and Telemetry: sends diagnostic data to Microsoft. Windows works without it.
Routes push messages for device management and telemetry. Safe to disable on a personal PC.
Downloaded Maps Manager. Only needed by the Maps app.
Retail demo mode used in shops.
Xbox services. Only needed for Xbox app sign-in, game saves and Game Pass features.
Shares Windows Media Player libraries on the network.
Geolocation service. Only needed by apps that use your location.
Phone service used by the Your Phone / Phone Link features.
Parental controls. Only needed if you use Family Safety on this PC.
Smart card support. Only needed if you use smart cards.
SNMP trap receiver for network management tools.
Touch keyboard and handwriting panel. Only needed with touch or pen input.
Bluetooth support. Disabling it turns off Bluetooth devices.
Print Spooler. Only needed if you print from this PC; disabling it reduces attack surface otherwise.
Windows Search indexing. Disabling makes searching files slower but frees some disk and CPU use.
SysMain (Superfetch) preloads apps. Mostly useful on hard disks; on SSDs it makes little difference.
Distributed Link Tracking Client. Only helps keep shortcuts working across network moves.
Mobile hotspot / Internet Connection Sharing. Only needed if you share this PC's connection.
Event collector for remote event subscriptions.
Windows Error Reporting. Disabling stops crash reports being sent to Microsoft.
AllJoyn router for Internet-of-Things apps.
Application Layer Gateway for connection sharing.
Program Compatibility Assistant. Disabling can stop older programs getting compatibility help.
Windows Insider Service. Only needed if you take Insider preview builds.
Wi-Fi Direct. Only needed for casting/sharing over Wi-Fi Direct.
Payments and NFC management.
Only needed on a work/school domain.
Work Folders sync. Only needed on a work network that uses it.
Lets several apps share the camera.
Network map discovery (Link-Layer Topology).
Peer-to-peer networking (HomeGroup-era). Rarely used.
Remote Desktop. Disable if you never connect to this PC remotely.
Windows Remote Management. Only needed for remote administration.
Discovers and hosts UPnP devices on the network.
Diagnostics hub collector used by developer tools.
Google updater. Disabling can leave Chrome out of date.
Adobe updater/licensing helper. Adobe apps still open.
Firefox background updater. Firefox updates when you open it.
Apple Bonjour discovery. Only needed by some Apple and printer software.
Apple iPod helper.
Needed to connect an iPhone/iPad to this PC. Disabling stops that connection.
Steam helper service. Steam asks for it when installing games.
Updates Microsoft Edge. Disabling can leave Edge out of date.
Microsoft Office updater/streaming. Disabling can leave Office out of date.
